To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) non-templated recombination is promoted by transcription and AIDA in human germinal center like B cells, and (ii) this activity may contribute to somatic hypermutaion in these cells.
non-conservative homologously directed DNA transactions are promoted by AID in human B lymphoma cells and that the activity of conservative homologous recombinases is low or absent.

non-conservative homologously recombined products are detected at elevated frequencies in human B cell lines, that this activity is enhanced by transcription and activation-induced cytidinedeaminase, and that conservative homologous recombinations are low to undetectable in these cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of somatic hypermutation (SHM).
the elucidation of the mechanisms of somatic mutation and gene conversion in B cells.
the elucidation of the molecular basis for Ig diversification and the role of AID and HR in the process of somatic hypermutation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AID is required for non-conservative HR in human B cells and that this pathway is promoted by transcription.

non-templated somatic hypermutation is not the result of a defect in the Ig gene conversion pathway but the result of a physiological suppression of the conservative Ig gene conversion pathway in germinal center B cells.
the non-conservative homologously recombined DNA repair mechanism is promoted by AID in human B cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AID and transcription promote non-conservative recombination in human germinal center like B cells.
non-conservative HR is promoted by AID in germinal centre cells and that this may be the basis for hypermutation in these cells.

AID is able to promote both conservative HR (gene conversion) and non-conservative HR, which may be a prerequisite to explain the differential usage of gene conversion and somatic hypermutation during B cell development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the activity of non-conservative HR in mammalian cells is not restricted to the Ig loci and that it is promoted by transcription and AIDs activity.
AID and transcription promote non-templated homologous re-combination (HR) in human B cells.
non-conservative HR is an active and physiologically relevant DNA repair pathway in human B cells.
